Hi Monica,

Thanks for taking the meeting yesterday. ScoutAI is preparing a small pilot (user-facing summarization and reranking workflows) and we need a clear baseline for cost modeling. Could you send your standard hosted API rates expressed per 1M tokens (separate input vs output), and a current list of supported/verified models (with notes on recommended model for low-latency vs high-quality)?

A few specifics that would help:
- Per-1M token price (input vs output) for your standard hosted tiers
- Any pilot or trial rate you offer for POCs
- Which models are available on hosted right now and any limits (max context, quantized variants)
- Typical med-latency numbers (p95) for 8k and 32k context runs for your recommended low-latency option

We're aiming for a 30-day pilot starting early Jan — estimated 4M input tokens / 6M output tokens over the period (mostly short prompts + longer generations). If you need more context on the workload I can attach sample traces.

Best,
Ethan

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Morris <ethan.m@scoutai.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pricing + model list for pilot

Hi Ethan — great to hear from you. Short answer up-front, then attachments with the matrix and a pilot path. Let me know if you'd like these numbers in a single spreadsheet.

Baseline hosted API (public rate table for standard seats):
- Input tokens: $0.35 per 1M tokens
- Output tokens: $1.10 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- These rates are for our default hosted tier (no reserved capacity). Streaming and function calls are priced on token usage only.
- For pilots we commonly provide a temporary pilot credit or a 10% trial discount on the first month for deals moving to a paid pilot — see proposed pilot section below.

Certified/verified models currently available on hosted (short guide):
- redwood-7b: low-latency option, good for short-turn user prompts, 8k context supported (quantized variants available). p95: ~90-140ms per token depending on prompt length.
- redwood-13b: balanced throughput/quality, 8k and 32k context supported (higher mem footprint). p95: ~150-250ms per token.
- redwood-70b: higher-quality, recommended for heavy summarization; available on hosted with limited concurrency for tenants. p95: ~300-600ms per token.
- open-llama-34b (community model): available for cost-sensitive workloads, slightly higher latency but cheaper in practice.
- embeddings-large: specialized embedding model (priced per 1k vectors; will share a separate rate sheet if you need embeddings).

Pilot path we recommend:
- 30-day pilot with a short trial discount: first 2 weeks at 10% off listed rates (code: SCOUT-PILOT-10), then standard rates after.
- If you commit to a minimum monthly usage > 50M tokens we can offer a volume discount (tiered; can discuss percent off based on exact commit).

I've attached: token_estimate.xlsx (simple calculator for your 4M/6M example) and a model_latency_matrix CSV with measured p95s across contexts (rough numbers, varies by seq length). Ben is cc'd and can provide an official rate sheet and contract path if you want to progress.

Next steps:
- Do you want us to provision a demo tenant for ScoutAI to run a small workload?
- If yes, confirm a start date and whether you prefer open models or one of the redwood variants for the pilot.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference
Monica.Patel@redwood.ai

Attachments: token_estimate.xlsx (stated), model_latency_matrix.csv (stated)

Ethan — looping in our solutions lead Laura for latency and concurrency specifics. Monica, attaching the matrix we run for context.

Quick answers to the items Ethan raised: 
- p95 ms/token (typical observed ranges, subject to workload):
  * redwood-7b: 8k ctx ~ 90-140 ms/token, 32k ctx ~ 130-220 ms/token
  * redwood-13b: 8k ctx ~ 150-230 ms/token, 32k ctx ~ 260-420 ms/token
- Concurrency: hosted tier supports burst concurrency up to ~120 concurrent small requests per tenant; if you need sustained high concurrency we recommend Reserved/Dedicated which we can size.
- Discounts: the pilot 10% is a one-time promotional discount for the initial month; commit-based discounts for Dedicated/reserved capacity are negotiated separately and do not stack with short-term promotional credits, but we can roll pilot credits into a commitment conversation (happy to make exceptions in contract).

Laura — can you add the recommended model for ScoutAI's mix (short prompts + long summaries) and confirm if quantized redwood-13b is a solid middle ground?

Thanks,
